texts: Dyskinesis is paradoxical systolic motion, the segment bulging outward while the rest of the ventricle contracts: D.

Intraoperative TEE grades each segment by its inward motion and thickening: normal (thickening above about 30 percent), mild hypokinesis (10 to 30 percent), severe hypokinesis (below 10 percent), akinesis (none) and dyskinesis (outward motion).
The numbers in the other options do not match this grading.
In the picture, the ring of dancers steps in on the beat; one steps in only a little, one stands still, and the disco dancer steps out.
A new wall motion abnormality on TEE is an early sign of ischaemia, often before the ECG changes.
Memory hook: DYS-kinesis, the DISCO dancer who steps out.
